input.step_by_step_reasoning: 1) Nodes: took the nine drawn services (S3, Step Functions, MediaConvert, Rekognition, Transcribe, Comprehend, DynamoDB, EC2, EKS). The speaker mentions 'another step function' for the AI stage, but the board shows a single Step Functions icon, so it is kept as one node. Lambdas are mentioned verbally as tasks inside the step function but are not drawn; the board shows a direct Step Functions -> DynamoDB arrow, so that edge is kept direct and the Lambdas are recorded in notes. The uploading user is a generic human actor with no drawn icon, so it is pruned; S3 is the system entry point. Reach Engine is drawn as a box containing EC2 and EKS, so both are kept as nodes annotated as Reach Engine. 2) Edges follow the drawn arrows: S3 -> Step Functions (upload trigger), Step Functions -> MediaConvert / Rekognition / Transcribe (orchestration), Step Functions -> DynamoDB (technical metadata), Rekognition -> DynamoDB, Transcribe -> Comprehend, Transcribe -> DynamoDB, Comprehend -> DynamoDB, and DynamoDB -> Reach Engine box. The last arrow points at the box as a whole, so it is represented as edges to both EC2 and EKS; no EC2-EKS edge is drawn or added. No MediaConvert -> DynamoDB edge is drawn or added. 3) Flows: flow 0 = ingest, proxy transcode and technical metadata; flow 1 = AI/ML metadata extraction; flow 2 = ingest of metadata from the temporary DynamoDB store into Reach Engine.

graph.name: Levels Beyond - Media to Cloud Workflow with Reach Engine
graph.categories: Media & Entertainment, Serverless, Machine Learning, Media Processing
graph.notes: Levels Beyond Media2Cloud workflow: a file uploaded to S3 triggers Step Functions, which creates a browser proxy with MediaConvert, extracts technical metadata, and runs Rekognition, Transcribe and Comprehend. All metadata lands in DynamoDB as a temporary store and is then ingested into the Reach Engine platform (EC2 and EKS) for playback, search and visualization.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Ingest bucket. The user uploads a media file (any format) here; the upload triggers the Step Functions workflow.

nodes.name: Step Functions
nodes.notes: Orchestrates the Media to Cloud workflow: kicks off the MediaConvert transcode, triggers Lambdas that extract checksums and technical metadata (frame rates, media info), then a further step function runs Rekognition and Transcribe.

nodes.name: Elemental MediaConvert
nodes.notes: Transcodes the uploaded media into a proxy suitable for browser playback, giving users a visual check alongside the extracted metadata.

nodes.name: Rekognition
nodes.notes: Analyzes the video to identify celebrities, violence, nudity and other content data; results are associated with time codes.

nodes.name: Transcribe
nodes.notes: Converts the audio of the content into text.

nodes.name: Comprehend
nodes.notes: Analyzes the transcribed text to extract entities and detect things such as profanity.

nodes.name: DynamoDB
nodes.notes: Temporary data store for technical metadata (checksums, frame rates, media info) and for Rekognition, Transcribe and Comprehend results. Once data is there, an ingest into Reach Engine is triggered.

nodes.name: Reach Engine (EC2)
nodes.notes: EC2 component of the Reach Engine platform, the core product: playback of ingested content, viewing and searching extracted metadata, celebrity track visualization, and feeding an orchestration engine to distribute content.

nodes.name: Reach Engine (EKS)
nodes.notes: EKS component of the Reach Engine platform, drawn alongside EC2 inside the Reach Engine box.

edges.notes: The file upload to the S3 bucket triggers the step function.
Step Functions first kicks off the transcode in MediaConvert to create a browser playback proxy.
After the proxy is generated, Lambdas triggered by the step function extract checksums and technical metadata (frame rates, media info) and store it in DynamoDB.
After the basic metadata is extracted, a further step function starts Rekognition on the video.
Rekognition results (celebrities, violence, nudity) with time codes are written to DynamoDB.
The same step function triggers Transcribe to convert audio to text.
The transcribed text is driven into Comprehend for analysis.
Transcription output is stored in DynamoDB.
Comprehend output (entities, profanity detection) is stored in DynamoDB.
Once the data is in DynamoDB, an ingest into Reach Engine is triggered; the arrow points to the Reach Engine box.
Same ingest into Reach Engine; the arrow targets the Reach Engine box, which contains both EC2 and EKS.
